2027-06-18.title: Friday of the fourth week after Pentecost · Mar Aprem Malpan (St Ephrem the Syrian)
readings: The law has only a shadow of the good things to come
I have called you friends; love one another as I have loved you
2027-06-18.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. The Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) is being kept; it ends with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June. The Panchangam keeps today the memory of Mar Aprem Malpan, St Ephrem the Syrian, deacon and Doctor of the Church.
2027-06-18.verse: I do not call you servants any longer, because the servant does not know what the master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.
theo: Today our Church keeps the memory of Mar Aprem Malpan, St Ephrem the Syrian, the greatest poet of our Syriac tradition. He was born at Nisibis in Mesopotamia at the beginning of the fourth century, served the Church there as a deacon and as a teacher of the faith, and when Nisibis was handed over to Persia in 363 he went with many Christians to Edessa, where he taught and wrote until his death in 373. He never became a priest or a bishop; he remained a deacon, a servant, all his life. Yet his hymns, the madrashe, taught the faith to whole peoples, and they are still sung in the prayers of the Syriac Churches, ours among them. He wrote them for choirs of women and girls, so that the doctrine of the Church might be carried home on melodies that people loved. The Syriac tradition calls him the Harp of the Spirit. In 1920 Pope Benedict XV declared him a Doctor of the universal Church. It is fitting that his memory falls in the Apostles' Fast: Ephrem was a man of fasting and prayer, and tradition remembers that in his last years, when famine struck Edessa, he left his cell to organise help for the hungry and the sick.

The Epistle of the day is a passage Ephrem would have loved. “Since the law has only a shadow of the good things to come and not the true form of these realities, it can never, by the same sacrifices that are continually offered year after year, make perfect those who approach.” The sacrifices of the old covenant were true worship given by God to Israel, but they were shadows cast ahead by the coming light. “For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.” Only the one offering of Christ does that. Ephrem saw the whole Bible and the whole of creation as full of such shadows and symbols, which our tradition calls raze, mysteries. The lamb, the ark, the manna, the rock in the desert, the dew, the pearl, the olive and its oil: everything, for him, was a window through which Christ could be seen. He wrote that the Word of God is like a living spring: whoever drinks from it takes only a little and leaves far more behind, and should give thanks for what he has received instead of grieving over what he could not take in (Commentary on the Diatessaron 1, in substance). That is how he read Scripture, with wonder and thanksgiving, never pretending to have exhausted it. And Ephrem sang tenderly of the holy Mother of God, through whom the reality came into the world. Addressing Christ, he wrote that only he and his Mother are beautiful in every way, for in him there is no blemish and in his Mother no stain (Nisibene Hymns 27, in substance).

The Gospel shows what the shadows were pointing to: not only a perfect sacrifice but a friendship. “This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. I do not call you servants any longer, because the servant does not know what the master is doing; but I have called you friends.” The old sacrifices could not make the worshippers perfect; the sacrifice of Christ makes servants into friends. And Jesus adds: “You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last.” Ephrem's fruit has lasted for sixteen centuries; every time the Syriac Churches sing his hymns, the friend of Christ is still bearing fruit. Ours may be smaller and hidden: a prayer taught to a child, a hymn sung with love, a meal given to a hungry neighbour. On this Friday of the fast, let us give thanks for the friendship Christ offers us, and ask Mar Aprem to teach us to sing it.
outline: Ask: do I relate to God as a servant afraid of his master, or as a friend who knows his heart?
Point 1 · The shadow and the true form
The old sacrifices were shadows; only Christ's offering takes away sin.
The sacrifice of the Cross makes servants into friends, and friends love one another.
Point 3 · The Harp of the Spirit
Mar Aprem saw Christ in every symbol of Scripture and creation, and sang the faith.
live: Take one Old Testament story you know, such as the manna or the Passover lamb, and ask in prayer how it points to Christ.
On this Friday of the fast, give a meal or its cost to someone who is hungry, as Mar Aprem did in the famine of Edessa.
2027-06-18.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, the shadows of the law have passed and you have come, the true and only sacrifice that takes away sin. You no longer call us servants but friends. Through the prayers of Mar Aprem Malpan, the Harp of the Spirit, open our eyes to see you in the Scriptures and in all your creation, teach us to praise you with joy, and make us love one another as you have loved us. Let our lives bear fruit that will last, to the glory of your Father and the Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen.
altar: What the sacrifices of the law could only foreshadow is given on our altar: in the Holy Qurbono the one offering of Christ is made present, and the Lord who laid down his life for his friends gives himself to us as food. Mar Aprem sang that in the bread there is hidden fire.
conn: Hebrews 10:5–10, read tomorrow, continues today's passage: Christ comes to do the Father's will, and we are sanctified through the offering of his body once for all.
John 15:1–10 comes just before today's Gospel: the friends of Jesus bear fruit only by remaining in him, as branches in the vine.
Exodus 33:11: the Lord spoke with Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend; in Christ that friendship is offered to all.
fathers: Who can grasp even one of your words, Lord? We leave behind far more than we take, like the thirsty who drink from a spring; let the one who drinks give thanks and not grieve that the spring is greater than his thirst (Commentary on the Diatessaron 1, in substance).
You alone, Lord, and your Mother are beautiful in every way: in you there is no blemish, and in your Mother no stain (Nisibene Hymns 27, in substance).
magis: The sacrifice of Christ is unique; it completes and surpasses all other sacrifices. It is first a gift from God the Father himself, and at the same time the offering of the Son who willingly and lovingly gives his life.

The beauty of images, music and song serves the Church's prayer; the harmony of signs, song, music, words and actions is more expressive and fruitful when it springs from the cultural richness of the people who pray.
St Ephrem is the most important witness of Syriac-speaking Christianity; he shows that theology can be done in poetry, and that poetry can be a way of praying and teaching the faith (in substance).

quick: Today we remember Mar Aprem Malpan, St Ephrem the Syrian, deacon, poet and Doctor of the Church, called the Harp of the Spirit.
Hebrews: the law has only a shadow of the good things to come; the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins.
Jesus: I do not call you servants any longer, but friends; love one another as I have loved you.
2027-06-18.action: Sing or read slowly one hymn of our liturgy today, and thank God for what it teaches.
2027-06-18.question: Do I know Jesus as a friend, or only as a master to be obeyed?

family.explain: Jesus tells his disciples that they are not his servants but his friends, and that the greatest love is to give your life for your friends. Today we remember Mar Aprem, a holy deacon who lived long ago in Syria. He loved Jesus so much that he wrote many beautiful songs about him, and he taught people to sing them. When there was a famine, he helped the hungry. He was a true friend of Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for all who teach the faith, especially through music and song.
family.ask: Ask: “What is your favourite hymn, and what does it tell us about Jesus?”

illus: In a parish in Thiruvalla, an old choir master used to begin every practice with the same words: we are not here to perform, we are here to pray twice. One evening a teenage girl asked him why the old Syriac melodies mattered when the young people preferred new songs. He answered with a story. Sixteen centuries ago, he said, a deacon named Ephrem noticed that heretics were teaching wrong ideas about Christ through catchy tunes. Instead of only arguing, he wrote better songs, true songs, and taught them to choirs of women, who sang them in the streets and the churches until the whole city knew the true faith by heart. Then the choir master said: every time you sing the hymns of our Church, you are carrying the faith home in a melody. The girl stayed in the choir, and years later she was teaching the hymns to children herself.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have called us your friends. With Mar Aprem, the Harp of the Spirit, we praise you; teach us to see you in your word and to love one another as you have loved us. Amen.
share: The law has only a shadow of the good things to come (Hebrews 10:1). Where in the Old Testament have I discovered Christ?
I have called you friends (John 15:15). What does friendship with Jesus mean in my daily life?
I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). What fruit is Jesus asking me to bear now?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your friendship.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may proclaim the one sacrifice of Christ and the friendship he offers to all.
For our Syriac Churches, Catholic and Orthodox, who love Mar Aprem, that his prayer may draw us to unity.
For deacons, catechists, choir members and all who teach the faith through word and song.
For the hungry and for those who suffer from famine and poverty, that they may find friends who help them.
For all who keep the Apostles' Fast, that their self-denial may bear fruit in love.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave your Church Mar Aprem Malpan, deacon and teacher, who sang your mysteries with the harp of the Spirit. Through his prayers, let us see your Son in every page of Scripture, love one another as he loved us, and bear fruit that will last. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: From the Syriac malpana, teacher. In the Syriac tradition it is the title of a learned teacher of the Scriptures and the faith; in Kerala it was given to the masters who taught Syriac and theology to future priests. Mar Aprem is called Malpan because his hymns and commentaries taught the whole Church.
kidsaint: Mar Aprem, the harp of the Holy Spirit

Long ago in Syria there lived a deacon named Ephrem, Aprem in our language. Some people were teaching wrong things about Jesus with songs that were easy to remember. Ephrem did not just argue with them. He wrote new songs, full of true and beautiful words about Jesus and Mother Mary, and taught them to choirs of women and girls. Soon the whole town was singing the true faith! People called him the harp of the Holy Spirit. Lesson: you can share your love for Jesus by singing.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember Mar Aprem Malpan, St Ephrem the Syrian. He was a deacon in Nisibis and Edessa in the fourth century, and he wrote hundreds of hymns that taught the faith. Our Syriac tradition calls him the Harp of the Spirit, and the whole Church honours him as a Doctor.

The Epistle says that the law has only a shadow of the good things to come (Hebrews 10:1). The old sacrifices pointed forward, but it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins (Hebrews 10:4). Only Jesus, by his one offering, takes away sin. Mar Aprem loved to find these shadows and symbols in Scripture and in nature, and to show how all of them point to Christ.

And what do they point to? To friendship. Jesus says: I do not call you servants any longer, but I have called you friends (John 15:15). No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends (John 15:13). On the Cross, Jesus made us his friends. And friends of Jesus must love one another as he loved us.

Mar Aprem was such a friend. He prayed, fasted, sang and, when famine came, cared for the hungry. In this Apostles' Fast, let us ask him to teach us to see Christ in the Scriptures, to praise him with joy, and to love one another in deeds. Amen.
kids: Children, do you like to sing? Today we remember a saint who loved to sing about Jesus: Mar Aprem. He lived long, long ago and wrote many, many songs to teach people about Jesus and Mother Mary. People called him the harp of the Holy Spirit, because his songs were like music played by God. Jesus says today: you are my friends. A friend of Jesus sings his praises and helps others. So today, sing a hymn for Jesus, and help someone who needs you.

intro: Theme: “I do not call you servants any longer… but I have called you friends.”
On the memory of Mar Aprem Malpan, in the Apostles' Fast: the shadow and the reality, the friendship of Christ, and the Harp of the Spirit.

sub: What the blood of animals could not do.

he entered once for all into the Holy Place, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.
points.apply: At the next Holy Qurbono, unite your own small sacrifices of the fast with the one offering of Christ.

sub: Chosen to bear fruit that will last.
q: Thus the Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.
We love because he first loved us.
points.apply: Speak to Jesus today for five minutes as to a friend, telling him plainly what is in your heart.

sub: Hymns that carried the faith home.
q: Awake, my soul! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awake the dawn.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; teach and admonish one another in all wisdom; and with gratitude in your hearts sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs to God.
points.apply: Learn by heart one hymn of our liturgy, or teach one to a child, this week.

concl: The shadows of the law led to Christ, and Christ leads us into friendship.
Mar Aprem sang that friendship for the whole Church; we are invited to live it and to sing it.
2027-06-18.resolve: Live as a friend of Jesus: love one another as he loved us, and praise him with your whole heart.
